Flow cytometry of bone marrow aspirate revealed a monoclonal B-cell population (kappa restricted) expressing CD19, CD20, CD22, HLA-DR, FMC7 with partial expression of CD25 and CD103. clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old male presented with incidentally discovered isolated mild thrombocytopenia (platelets 120K/μL) with otherwise normal complete blood count including normal hemoglobin (15.4 g/dL), hematocrit (45.7%), and WBC (4.2 K/μL). Approximately three weeks after the initial presentation, bone marrow evaluation was performed. Bone marrow aspirate flow cytometry revealed a monoclonal kappa light chain-restricted B-cell population comprising 34% of total cells and 41% of lymphocytes, expressing CD19, CD20, CD22, HLA-DR, FMC7, with partial positivity for CD25 and CD103. Bone marrow core biopsy demonstrated normocellular marrow with 30-40% infiltration by medium-sized mature B-cells with oval-shaped nuclei, abundant cytoplasm, and characteristic cytoplasmic projections (hairy cells). Immunohistochemical staining confirmed the diagnostic profile: positive for CD20, Annexin A1, DBA44, BCL1, BCL2, TRAP, and BRAF V600E mutation, with negative staining for CD5, CD10, LEF1, and BCL6, effectively excluding chronic lymphocytic leukemia, follicular lymphoma, and mantle cell lymphoma.
